children.text: Chapter 1
janaka uvāca
children.translated_text: <s>Janaka</s> said:

children.text: kathaṃ jñānam avāpnoti kathaṃ muktir bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: How does one obtain knowledge? How will liberation come about?

children.text: vairāgyaṃ ca kathaṃ prāptam etad brūhi mama prabho ||
children.translated_text: And how is dispassion attained? Tell me this, my lord.

children.text: aṣṭāvakra uvāca
children.translated_text: <s>Aṣṭāvakra</s> said:

children.text: muktim icchasi cet tāta viṣayān viṣavat tyaja
children.translated_text: If you desire liberation, dear one, abandon sense-objects as if they were poison.

children.text: kṣamārjavadayātoṣasatyaṃ pīyūṣavad bhaja ||
children.translated_text: Cultivate forgiveness, straightforwardness, compassion, contentment, and truth as if they were nectar.

children.text: na pṛthvī na jalaṃ nāgnir na vāyur dyaur na vā bhavān
children.translated_text: You are not earth, not water, not fire, not wind, nor are you sky.

children.text: eṣāṃ sākṣiṇam ātmānaṃ cidrūpaṃ viddhi muktaye ||
children.translated_text: Know the self as the witness of these, whose form is consciousness, for the sake of liberation.

children.text: yadi dehaṃ pṛthak kṛtya citi viśrāmya tiṣṭhasi
children.translated_text: If, having separated yourself from the body, you rest in consciousness and remain there,

children.text: adhunaiva sukhī śānto bandhamukto bhaviṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: this very moment you will be happy, peaceful, and freed from bondage.

children.text: na tvaṃ viprādiko varṇo nāśramī nākṣagocaraḥ
children.translated_text: You are not a social class such as a brahmin, nor an āśrama (stage of life), nor an object of the senses.

children.text: asaṅgo 'si nirākāro viśvasākṣī sukhī bhava ||
children.translated_text: You are unattached, formless, the witness of the universe; be happy.

children.text: dharmādharmau sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ mānasāni na te vibho
children.translated_text: Dharma and adharma, pleasure and pain, are mental constructs; they are not yours, all-pervading one.

children.text: na kartāsi na bhoktāsi mukta evāsi sarvadā ||
children.translated_text: You are not the doer and not the enjoyer; you are always liberated indeed.

children.text: eko draṣṭāsi sarvasya muktaprāyo 'si sarvadā
children.translated_text: You are the one seer of everything; you are always virtually free.

children.text: ayam eva hi te bandho draṣṭāraṃ paśyasītaram ||
children.translated_text: This alone is your bondage: that you see the seer as something other.

children.text: ahaṃ kartety ahaṃmānamahākṛṣṇāhidaṃśitaḥ
children.translated_text: Bitten by the great black serpent of egoism, the conceit 'I am the doer,'

children.text: nāhaṃ karteti viśvāsāmṛtaṃ pītvā sukhī bhava ||
children.translated_text: drink the nectar of the conviction 'I am not the doer,' and be happy.

children.text: eko viśuddhabodho 'ham iti niścayavahninā
children.translated_text: With the fire of certainty, 'I am one, pure awareness,'

children.text: prajvālyājñānagahanaṃ vītaśokaḥ sukhī bhava ||
children.translated_text: burn up the dense forest of ignorance; free from sorrow, be happy.

children.text: yatra viśvam idaṃ bhāti kalpitaṃ rajjusarpavat
children.translated_text: Where this universe shines forth, imagined like a snake in a rope,

children.text: ānandaparamānandaḥ sa bodhas tvaṃ sukhaṃ cara ||
children.translated_text: that awareness, bliss and supreme bliss, is you; move happily.

children.text: muktābhimānī mukto hi baddho baddhābhimāny api
children.translated_text: One who identifies as liberated is liberated; one who identifies as bound is bound as well.

children.text: kiṃvadantīha satyeyaṃ yā matiḥ sā gatir bhavet ||
children.translated_text: This saying here is true: as one's thought is, so one's destination becomes.

children.text: ātmā sākṣī vibhuḥ pūrṇa eko muktaś cid akriyaḥ
children.translated_text: The self is witness, all-pervading, complete, one, free, consciousness, and inactive.

children.text: asaṅgo nispṛhaḥ śānto bhramāt saṃsāravān iva ||
children.translated_text: It is unattached, desireless, and peaceful, yet through delusion it seems to possess saṃsāra.

children.text: kūṭasthaṃ bodham advaitam ātmānaṃ paribhāvaya
children.translated_text: Contemplate the self as immutable, awareness, and nondual.

children.text: ābhāso 'haṃ bhramaṃ muktvā bhāvaṃ bāhyam athāntaraṃ ||
children.translated_text: Abandon the delusion 'I am an appearance,' and abandon both the external and internal condition.

children.text: dehābhimānapāśena ciraṃ baddho 'si putraka
children.translated_text: You have long been bound, my child, by the noose of identification with the body.

children.text: bodho 'haṃ jñānakhaḍgena tan niṣkṛtya sukhī bhava ||
children.translated_text: Cut it with the sword of knowledge, 'I am awareness,' and be happy.

children.text: niḥsaṅgo niṣkriyo 'si tvaṃ svaprakāśo nirañjanaḥ
children.translated_text: You are without attachment and without action; you are self-luminous and stainless.

children.text: ayam eva hi te bandhaḥ samādhim anutiṣṭhasi ||
children.translated_text: This alone is your bondage: that you practice samādhi.

children.text: tvayā vyāptam idaṃ viśvaṃ tvayi protaṃ yathārthataḥ
children.translated_text: This universe is pervaded by you; in truth it is woven upon you.

children.text: śuddhabuddhasvarūpas tvaṃ mā gamaḥ kṣudracittatām ||
children.translated_text: You are pure awakened being itself; do not fall into small-mindedness.

children.text: nirapekṣo nirvikāro nirbharaḥ śītalāśayaḥ
children.translated_text: Be independent, changeless, self-sufficient, with a cool inner disposition,

children.text: agādhabuddhir akṣubdho bhava cinmātravāsanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: of unfathomable intelligence, unagitated, intent only on consciousness.

children.text: sākāram anṛtaṃ viddhi nirākāraṃ tu niścalam
children.translated_text: Know what has form to be unreal, but the formless to be unmoving.

children.text: etattattvopadeśena na punarbhavasambhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Through this instruction in reality, there is no possibility of rebirth.

children.text: yathaivādarśamadhyasthe rūpe 'ntaḥ paritas tu saḥ
children.translated_text: Just as, when an image is placed in the middle of a mirror, the mirror is within and all around it,

children.text: tathaivāsmin śarīre 'ntaḥ paritaḥ parameśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: so in this body, within and all around, is the supreme Lord.

children.text: ekaṃ sarvagataṃ vyoma bahir antar yathā ghaṭe
children.translated_text: Just as one all-pervading space is outside and inside a pot,

children.text: nityaṃ nirantaraṃ brahma sarvabhūtagaṇe tathā ||
children.translated_text: so eternal, uninterrupted brahman is in the whole multitude of beings.

children.text: Chapter 2
janaka uvāca
children.translated_text: <s>Janaka</s> said:

children.text: aho nirañjanaḥ śānto bodho 'haṃ prakṛteḥ paraḥ
children.translated_text: Ah! I am stainless, peaceful awareness, beyond prakṛti (primordial nature).

children.text: etāvantam ahaṃ kālaṃ mohenaiva viḍambitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For all this time I have been mocked by delusion alone.

children.text: yathā prakāśayāmy eko deham enaṃ tathā jagat
children.translated_text: Just as I alone illuminate this body, so too I illuminate the world.

children.text: ato mama jagat sarvam athavā na ca kiṃcana ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the whole world is mine, or else nothing at all is.

children.text: saśarīram aho viśvaṃ parityajya mayādhunā
children.translated_text: Ah! Having now abandoned the universe together with the body,

children.text: kutaścit kauśalād eva paramātmā vilokyate ||
children.translated_text: by some skill alone the supreme self is seen.

children.text: yathā na toyato bhinnās taraṅgāḥ phenabudbudāḥ
children.translated_text: Just as waves, foam, and bubbles are not different from water,

children.text: ātmano na tathā bhinnaṃ viśvam ātmavinirgatam ||
children.translated_text: so the universe, issuing from the self, is not different from the self.

children.text: tantumātro bhaved eva paṭo yadvad vicāritaḥ
children.translated_text: Just as, when examined, a cloth is nothing but thread,

children.text: ātmatanmatram evedaṃ tadvad viśvaṃ vicāritam ||
children.translated_text: so, when examined, this universe is nothing but the self.

children.text: yathaivekṣurase kﾱptā tena vyāptaiva śarkarā
children.translated_text: Just as sugar produced in sugarcane juice is completely pervaded by it,

children.text: tathā viśvaṃ mayi kﾱptaṃ mayā vyāptaṃ nirantaram ||
children.translated_text: so the universe, projected in me, is pervaded by me without interruption.

children.text: ātmājñānāj jagad bhāti ātmajñānān na bhāsate
children.translated_text: From ignorance of the self the world appears; from knowledge of the self it does not appear.

children.text: rajjvajñānād ahir bhāti tajjñānād bhāsate na hi ||
children.translated_text: From ignorance of the rope a snake appears; from knowledge of that, it surely does not appear.

children.text: prakāśo me nijaṃ rūpaṃ nātirikto 'smy ahaṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: Light is my own nature; I am not other than that.

children.text: yadā prakāśate viśvaṃ tadāham bhāsa eva hi ||
children.translated_text: When the universe shines forth, then it is I alone who shine.

children.text: aho vikalpitaṃ viśvam ajñānān mayi bhāsate
children.translated_text: Ah! Through ignorance the imagined universe appears in me,

children.text: rūpyaṃ śuktau phaṇī rajjau vāri sūryakare yathā ||
children.translated_text: like silver in mother-of-pearl, a serpent in a rope, or water in a sunbeam.

children.text: matto vinirgataṃ viśvaṃ mayy eva layam eṣyati
children.translated_text: The universe that has come forth from me will dissolve in me alone,

children.text: mṛdi kumbho jale vīciḥ kanake kaṭakaṃ yathā ||
children.translated_text: like a pot in clay, a wave in water, or a bracelet in gold.

children.text: aho ahaṃ namo mahyaṃ vināśo yasya nāsti me
children.translated_text: Ah, I! Reverence to myself, for there is no destruction of me,

children.text: brahmādistambaparyantaṃ jagannāśe 'pi tiṣṭhataḥ ||
children.translated_text: who remain even at the destruction of the world, from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a clump of grass.

children.text: aho ahaṃ namo mahyaṃ eko 'haṃ dehavān api
children.translated_text: Ah, I! Reverence to myself. Though embodied, I am one.

children.text: kvacin na gantā nāgantā vyāpya viśvam avasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I do not go anywhere and do not come from anywhere; I remain pervading the universe.

children.text: aho ahaṃ namo mahyaṃ dakṣo nāstīha matsamaḥ
children.translated_text: Ah, I! Reverence to myself. There is no one here as capable as I,

children.text: asaṃspṛśya śarīreṇa yena viśvaṃ ciraṃ dhṛtam ||
children.translated_text: by whom the universe has long been sustained without touching it with the body.

children.text: aho ahaṃ namo mahyaṃ yasya me nāsti kiṃcana
children.translated_text: Ah, I! Reverence to myself, to whom nothing belongs,

children.text: athavā yasya me sarvaṃ yad vāṅmanasagocaram ||
children.translated_text: or else to whom everything belongs that is within the range of speech and mind.

children.text: jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ tathā jñātā tritayaṃ nāsti vāstavam
children.translated_text: Knowledge, the knowable, and the knower: this triad is not real.

children.text: ajñānād bhāti yatredaṃ so 'ham asmi nirañjanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I am that stainless one in whom this appears through ignorance.

children.text: dvaitamūlam aho duḥkhaṃ nānyat tasyāsti bheṣajam
children.translated_text: Ah! Suffering has duality as its root; there is no other remedy for it.

children.text: dṛśyam etan mṛṣā sarvaṃ eko 'haṃ cidraso 'malaḥ ||
children.translated_text: All this seen world is false; I alone am the stainless essence of consciousness.

children.text: bodhamātro 'ham ajñānād upadhiḥ kalpito mayā
children.translated_text: I am mere awareness; through ignorance an adjunct has been imagined by me.

children.text: evaṃ vimṛśato nityaṃ nirvikalpe sthitir mama ||
children.translated_text: For one who constantly reflects in this way, my abiding is in the nonconceptual.

children.text: na me bandho 'sti mokṣo vā bhrāntiḥ śāntā nirāśrayā
children.translated_text: For me there is no bondage or liberation; delusion, without support, has become quiet.

children.text: aho mayi sthitaṃ viśvaṃ vastuto na mayi sthitam ||
children.translated_text: Ah, the universe abides in me, though in reality it does not abide in me.

children.text: saśarīram idaṃ viśvaṃ na kiṃcid iti niścitam
children.translated_text: This universe, together with the body, is certainly nothing at all.

children.text: śuddhacinmātra ātmā ca tat kasmin kalpanādhunā ||
children.translated_text: And the self is mere pure consciousness; so in what can there now be imagination?

children.text: śarīraṃ svarganarakau bandhamokṣau bhayaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: The body, heaven and hell, bondage and liberation, and fear as well,

children.text: kalpanāmātram evaitat kiṃ me kāryaṃ cidātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: all this is only imagination. What business is there for me, whose self is consciousness?

children.text: aho janasamūhe 'pi na dvaitaṃ paśyato mama
children.translated_text: Ah, even in a crowd of people I see no duality.

children.text: araṇyam iva saṃvṛttaṃ kva ratiṃ karavāṇy aham ||
children.translated_text: It has become like a forest; where shall I take delight?

children.text: nāham deho na me deho jīvo nāham ahaṃ hi cit
children.translated_text: I am not the body, nor is the body mine; I am not the living individual, for I am consciousness.

children.text: ayam eva hi me bandha āsīt yā jīvite spṛhā ||
children.translated_text: This alone was my bondage: the desire I had for life.

children.text: aho bhuvanakallolair vicitrair drāk samutthitam
children.translated_text: Ah, by the varied waves of worlds it has suddenly arisen

children.text: mayy anantamahāmbhodhau cittavāte samudyate ||
children.translated_text: in me, the infinite great ocean, when the wind of the mind arises.

children.text: mayy anantamahāmbhodhau cittavāte praśāmyati
children.translated_text: In me, the infinite great ocean, when the wind of the mind grows quiet,

children.text: abhāgyāj jīvavaṇijo jagat poto vinaśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: through misfortune the merchant who is the living being, with the boat that is the world, perishes.

children.text: mayy anantamahāmbhodhāvāścaryaṃ jīvavīcayaḥ
children.translated_text: In me, the infinite great ocean, wonder of wonders, the waves that are living beings

children.text: udyanti ghnanti khelanti praviśanti svabhāvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: arise, strike one another, play, and enter back by their own nature.

children.text: Chapter 3
aṣṭāvakra uvāca
children.translated_text: <s>Aṣṭāvakra</s> said:

children.text: avināśinam ātmānam ekaṃ vijñāya tattvataḥ
children.translated_text: Having known the self truly as imperishable and one,

children.text: tavātmajñasya dhīrasya katham arthārjane ratiḥ ||
children.translated_text: how can there be delight in acquiring wealth for you, a steadfast knower of the self?

children.text: ātmājñānād aho prītir viṣayabhramagocare
children.translated_text: Ah, from ignorance of the self comes fondness for the domain of delusive objects,

children.text: śukter ajñānato lobho yathā rajatavibhrame ||
children.translated_text: just as, from ignorance of mother-of-pearl, greed arises in the delusion of silver.

children.text: viśvaṃ sphurati yatredaṃ taraṅgā iva sāgare
children.translated_text: Knowing, 'I am that in which this universe shines forth like waves in the ocean,'

children.text: so 'ham asmīti vijñāya kiṃ dīna iva dhāvasi ||
children.translated_text: why do you run about like a wretched man?

children.text: śrutvāpi śuddhacaitanyam ātmānam atisundaram
children.translated_text: Even after hearing that the self is pure consciousness and exceedingly beautiful,

children.text: upasthetyantasaṃsakto mālinyam adhigacchati ||
children.translated_text: one who is utterly attached to the sexual organ comes to impurity.

children.text: sarvabhūteṣu cātmānaṃ sarvabhūtāni cātmani
children.translated_text: That a sage, knowing the self in all beings and all beings in the self,

children.text: muner jānata āścaryaṃ mamatvam anuvartate ||
children.translated_text: should still continue in possessiveness is astonishing.

children.text: āsthitaḥ paramādvaitaṃ mokṣārthe 'pi vyavasthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Established in supreme nonduality and resolved even upon liberation,

children.text: āścaryaṃ kāmavaśago vikalaḥ keliśikṣayā ||
children.translated_text: it is astonishing that one becomes subject to desire, agitated by instruction in dalliance.

children.text: udbhūtaṃ jñānadurmitram avadhāryātidurbalaḥ
children.translated_text: Though he has discerned that desire, the enemy of knowledge, has arisen, being extremely weak,

children.text: āścaryaṃ kāmam ākāṅkṣet kālam antam anuśritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: it is astonishing that one should long for desire, while following death as the end.

children.text: ihāmutra viraktasya nityānityavivekinaḥ
children.translated_text: For one detached from here and hereafter, discriminating between the eternal and the non-eternal,

children.text: āścaryaṃ mokṣakāmasya mokṣād eva vibhīṣikā ||
children.translated_text: it is astonishing that one who desires liberation should fear liberation itself.

children.text: dhīras tu bhojyamāno 'pi pīḍyamāno 'pi sarvadā
children.translated_text: But the steadfast one, even while being fed or even while being tormented, always

children.text: ātmānaṃ kevalaṃ paśyan na tuṣyati na kupyati ||
children.translated_text: sees only the self and is neither pleased nor angry.

children.text: ceṣṭamānaṃ śarīraṃ svaṃ paśyaty anyaśarīravat
children.translated_text: He sees his own body acting as if it were another body.

children.text: saṃstave cāpi nindāyāṃ kathaṃ kṣubhyet mahāśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: How could the great-souled one be disturbed by praise or by blame?

children.text: māyāmātram idaṃ viśvaṃ paśyan vigatakautukaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing this universe as mere illusion, with curiosity gone,

children.text: api saṃnihite mṛtyau kathaṃ trasyati dhīradhīḥ ||
children.translated_text: how can the steadfast-minded one tremble even when death is near?

children.text: niḥspṛhaṃ mānasaṃ yasya nairāśye 'pi mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: For the great-souled one whose mind is without craving even amid despair,

children.text: tasyātmajñānatṛptasya tulanā kena jāyate ||
children.translated_text: satisfied by knowledge of the self, with whom can any comparison be made?

children.text: svabhāvād eva jānāno dṛśyam etan na kiṃcana
children.translated_text: Knowing by his very nature that this visible world is nothing at all,

children.text: idaṃ grāhyam idaṃ tyājyaṃ sa kiṃ paśyati dhīradhīḥ ||
children.translated_text: what does the steadfast-minded one see as 'this is to be accepted' and 'this is to be rejected'?

children.text: antastyaktakaṣāyasya nirdvandvasya nirāśiṣaḥ
children.translated_text: For one whose inner impurity has been abandoned, who is free from dualities and without expectations,

children.text: yadṛcchayāgato bhogo na duḥkhāya na tuṣṭaye ||
children.translated_text: an enjoyment that comes by chance is neither for sorrow nor for satisfaction.

children.text: Chapter 4
aṣṭāvakra uvāca
children.translated_text: <s>Aṣṭāvakra</s> said:

children.text: hantātmajñasya dhīrasya khelato bhogalīlayā
children.translated_text: Alas, for the steadfast knower of the self, playing through the sport of enjoyments,

children.text: na hi saṃsāravāhīkair mūḍhaiḥ saha samānatā ||
children.translated_text: there is certainly no equality with fools who carry the burden of saṃsāra.

children.text: yat padaṃ prepsavo dīnāḥ śakrādyāḥ sarvadevatāḥ
children.translated_text: That state which the poor gods, <s>Śakra</s> and the rest, long to attain,

children.text: aho tatra sthito yogī na harṣam upagacchati ||
children.translated_text: ah, established there, the yogin does not come to exultation.

children.text: tajjñasya puṇyapāpābhyāṃ sparśo hy antar na jāyate
children.translated_text: For one who knows that, no inward contact with merit or demerit arises,

children.text: na hy ākāśasya dhūmena dṛśyamānāpi saṅgati ||
children.translated_text: for there is no real connection of smoke with space, even though it is seen.

children.text: ātmaivedaṃ jagat sarvaṃ jñātaṃ yena mahātmanā
children.translated_text: Who could be able to restrain that great-souled one by whom it is known that the self alone is this whole world,

children.text: yadṛcchayā vartamānaṃ taṃ niṣeddhuṃ kṣameta kaḥ ||
children.translated_text: as he lives according to what comes by chance?

children.text: ā brahmastambaparyante bhūtagrāme caturvidhe
children.translated_text: Among the fourfold host of beings, from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a clump of grass,

children.text: vijñasyaiva hi sāmarthyam icchānicchāvivarjane ||
children.translated_text: the power to be free from desire and aversion belongs only to the wise one.

children.text: ātmānam advayaṃ kaścij jānāti jagad īśvaraṃ
children.translated_text: Some rare person knows the self as nondual, the lord of the world.

children.text: yad vetti tat sa kurute na bhayaṃ tasya kutracit ||
children.translated_text: He does what he knows to be right; there is no fear for him anywhere.

children.text: Chapter 5
aṣṭāvakra uvāca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Aṣṭāvakra</s> said:

children.text: na te saṅgo 'sti kenāpi kiṃ śuddhas tyaktum icchasi
children.translated_text: You have no attachment to anything at all; being pure, what do you wish to abandon?

children.text: saṅghātavilayaṃ kurvann evam eva layaṃ vraja ||
children.translated_text: Bringing about the dissolution of the aggregate, enter dissolution just as you are.

children.text: udeti bhavato viśvaṃ vāridher iva budbudaḥ
children.translated_text: The universe rises from you like a bubble from the ocean.

children.text: iti jñātvaikam ātmānam evam eva layaṃ vraja ||
children.translated_text: Knowing the self thus as one, enter dissolution just as you are.

children.text: pratyakṣam apy avastutvād viśvaṃ nāsty amale tvayi
children.translated_text: Though directly perceived, because it has no reality, the universe does not exist in you, the stainless one,

children.text: rajjusarpa iva vyaktam evam eva layaṃ vraja ||
children.translated_text: plainly like a snake in a rope. Enter dissolution just as you are.

children.text: samaduḥkhasukhaḥ pūrṇa āśānairāśyayoḥ samaḥ
children.translated_text: Equal in pain and pleasure, complete, the same in hope and despair,

children.text: samajīvitamṛtyuḥ sann evam eva layaṃ vraja ||
children.translated_text: the same in life and death, enter dissolution just as you are.

children.text: Chapter 6
aṣṭāvakra uvāca
children.translated_text: <s>Aṣṭāvakra</s> said:

children.text: ākāśavad ananto 'haṃ ghaṭavat prakṛtaṃ jagat
children.translated_text: I am infinite like space; the manifest world is like a pot.

children.text: iti jñānaṃ tathaitasya na tyāgo na graho layaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This is knowledge. For this, there is no abandonment, no grasping, and no dissolution.

children.text: mahodadhir ivāhaṃ sa prapañco vīcisaṃnibhaḥ
children.translated_text: I am like the great ocean; this phenomenal expansion is like a wave.

children.text: iti jñānaṃ tathaitasya na tyāgo na graho layaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This is knowledge. For this, there is no abandonment, no grasping, and no dissolution.

children.text: ahaṃ sa śuktisaṅkāśo rūpyavad viśvakalpanā
children.translated_text: I am like mother-of-pearl; the imagination of the universe is like silver.

children.text: iti jñānaṃ tathaitasya na tyāgo na graho layaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This is knowledge. For this, there is no abandonment, no grasping, and no dissolution.

children.text: ahaṃ vā sarvabhūteṣu sarvabhūtāny atho mayi
children.translated_text: Either I am in all beings, and all beings are also in me.

children.text: iti jñānaṃ tathaitasya na tyāgo na graho layaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This is knowledge. For this, there is no abandonment, no grasping, and no dissolution.

children.text: Chapter 7
janaka uvāca
children.translated_text: <s>Janaka</s> said:

children.text: mayy anantamahāmbhodhau viśvapota itastataḥ
children.translated_text: In me, the infinite great ocean, the boat of the universe here and there

children.text: bhramati svāntavātena na mamāsty asahiṣṇutā ||
children.translated_text: wanders by the wind of its own inner faculty; I have no intolerance of it.

children.text: mayy anantamahāmbhodhau jagadvīciḥ svabhāvataḥ
children.translated_text: In me, the infinite great ocean, the wave of the world arises by its own nature.

children.text: udetu vastam āyātu na me vṛddhir na ca kṣatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let it arise, let it come to rest; for me there is neither increase nor loss.

children.text: mayy anantamahāmbhodhau viśvaṃ nāma vikalpanā
children.translated_text: In me, the infinite great ocean, what is called the universe is a mere conceptual construction.

children.text: atiśānto nirākāra etad evāham āsthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I am utterly peaceful and formless; in just this I remain established.

children.text: nātmā bhāveṣu no bhāvas tatrānante nirañjane
children.translated_text: The self is not in objects, nor are objects in that infinite, stainless one.

children.text: ity asakto 'spṛhaḥ śānta etad evāham āsthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus unattached, free from longing, and peaceful, I remain established in just this.

children.text: aho cinmātram evāham indrajālopamaṃ jagat
children.translated_text: Ah! I am nothing but consciousness; the world is like a magic show.

children.text: ato mama kathaṃ kutra heyopādeyakalpanā ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, how and where could there be for me any conception of what is to be rejected or accepted?

children.text: Chapter 8
aṣṭāvakra uvāca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Aṣṭāvakra</s> said:

children.text: tadā bandho yadā cittaṃ kiṃcid vāñchati śocati
children.translated_text: There is bondage when the mind desires something or grieves over something,

children.text: kiṃcin muñcati gṛhṇāti kiṃciddhṛṣyati kupyati ||
children.translated_text: when it gives something up, takes something up, rejoices over something, or becomes angry at something.

children.text: tadā muktir yadā cittaṃ na vāñchati na śocati
children.translated_text: There is liberation when the mind does not desire and does not grieve,

children.text: na muñcati na gṛhṇāti na hṛṣyati na kupyati ||
children.translated_text: does not give up, does not take up, does not rejoice, and does not become angry.

children.text: tadā bandho yadā cittaṃ saktaṃ kāsvapi dṛṣṭiṣu
children.translated_text: There is bondage when the mind is attached to any views whatsoever.

children.text: tadā mokṣo yadā cittam asaktaṃ sarvadṛṣṭiṣu ||
children.translated_text: There is mokṣa (liberation) when the mind is unattached to all views.

children.text: yadā nāhaṃ tadā mokṣo yadāhaṃ bandhanaṃ tadā
children.translated_text: When there is no 'I,' then there is mokṣa; when there is 'I,' then there is bondage.

children.text: matveti helayā kiṃcit mā gṛhāṇa vimuñca mā ||
children.translated_text: Knowing this, with indifference do not grasp anything and do not abandon anything.

children.text: Chapter 9
aṣṭāvakra uvāca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Aṣṭāvakra</s> said:

children.text: kṛtākṛte ca dvandvāni kadā śāntāni kasya vā
children.translated_text: For whom, and when, have the dualities of what has been done and not done ever become peaceful?

children.text: evaṃ jñātveha nirvedād bhava tyāgaparo 'vratī ||
children.translated_text: Knowing this here, through dispassion become intent on renunciation, free from vows.

children.text: kasyāpi tāta dhanyasya lokaceṣṭāvalokanāt
children.translated_text: For some blessed person, dear one, from observing the activities of the world,

children.text: jīvitecchā bubhukṣā ca bubhutsopaśamaḥ gatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the desire to live, hunger, and the wish to know have come to cessation.

children.text: anityaṃ sarvam evedaṃ tāpatritayadūṣitam
children.translated_text: All this is certainly impermanent, spoiled by the threefold suffering,

children.text: asāraṃ ninditaṃ heyam iti niścitya śāmyati ||
children.translated_text: without essence, blameworthy, and to be rejected; having determined this, one becomes peaceful.

children.text: ko 'sau kālo vayaḥ kiṃ vā yatra dvandvāni no nṛṇām
children.translated_text: What time is there, or what age, in which dualities are not present for human beings?

children.text: tāny upekṣya yathāprāptavartī siddhim avāpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: Disregarding them, one who lives with whatever comes to hand may attain perfection.

children.text: nānā mataṃ maharṣīṇāṃ sādhūnāṃ yogināṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Seeing the diverse opinions of great seers, good people, and yogins as well,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā nirvedam āpannaḥ ko na śāmyati mānavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: what human being, having attained dispassion, would not become peaceful?

children.text: kṛtvā mūrtiparijñānaṃ caitanyasya na kiṃ guruḥ
children.translated_text: Is he not a guru, who, having realized the nature of consciousness,

children.text: nirvedasamatāyuktyā yas tārayati saṃsṛteḥ ||
children.translated_text: carries one across saṃsṛti (worldly wandering) by means of dispassion and equanimity?

children.text: paśya bhūtavikārāṃs tvaṃ bhūtamātrān yathārthataḥ
children.translated_text: See the transformations of the elements as nothing but elements, just as they really are.

children.text: tatkṣaṇād bandhanirmuktaḥ svarūpastho bhaviṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: At that very moment, freed from bondage, you will abide in your own true nature.

children.text: vāsanā eva saṃsāra iti sarvā vimuñca tāḥ
children.translated_text: Vāsanās (latent tendencies) alone are saṃsāra; therefore abandon all of them.

children.text: tattyāgo vāsanātyāgāt sthitir adya yathā tathā ||
children.translated_text: From abandoning them, from abandoning the vāsanās, there is standing firm today just as you are.

children.text: Chapter 10
aṣṭāvakra uvāca
children.translated_text: <s>Aṣṭāvakra</s> said:

children.text: vihāya vairiṇaṃ kāmam arthaṃ cānarthasaṅkulam
children.translated_text: Having abandoned kāma (desire), your enemy, and artha (wealth), crowded with misfortune,

children.text: dharmam apy etayor hetuṃ sarvatrānādaraṃ kuru ||
children.translated_text: and even dharma, the cause of those two, cultivate disregard everywhere.

children.text: svapnendrajālavat paśya dināni trīṇi pañca vā
children.translated_text: See as like a dream or a magic show the prosperities of three or five days:

children.text: mitrakṣetradhanāgāradāradāyādisampadaḥ ||
children.translated_text: friends, fields, wealth, houses, wives, inheritances, and the like.

children.text: yatra yatra bhavet tṛṣṇā saṃsāraṃ viddhi tatra vai
children.translated_text: Wherever there may be thirsting desire, know saṃsāra to be right there.

children.text: prauḍhavairāgyam āśritya vītatṛṣṇaḥ sukhī bhava ||
children.translated_text: Relying on mature dispassion, become free from thirsting desire and happy.

children.text: tṛṣṇāmātrātmako bandhas tannāśo mokṣa ucyate
children.translated_text: Bondage consists only of thirsting desire; its destruction is called mokṣa.

children.text: bhāvasaṃsaktimātreṇa prāptituṣṭir muhurmuhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Through mere attachment to states, there is again and again contentment in acquisition.

children.text: tvam ekaś cetanaḥ śuddho jaḍaṃ viśvam asat tathā
children.translated_text: You alone are conscious and pure; the universe is inert and also unreal.

children.text: avidyāpi na kiṃcit sā kā bubhutsā tathāpi te ||
children.translated_text: Even avidyā (ignorance) is nothing at all; so what wish to know can you still have?

children.text: rājyaṃ sutāḥ kalatrāṇi śarīrāṇi sukhāni ca
children.translated_text: Kingdoms, sons, wives, bodies, and pleasures

children.text: saṃsaktasyāpi naṣṭāni tava janmani janmani ||
children.translated_text: have been lost by you birth after birth, though you were attached to them.

children.text: alam arthena kāmena sukṛtenāpi karmaṇā
children.translated_text: Enough of wealth, desire, and even meritorious action.

children.text: ebhyaḥ saṃsārakāntāre na viśrāntam abhūn manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: From these, in the wilderness of saṃsāra, the mind has found no rest.

children.text: kṛtaṃ na kati janmāni kāyena manasā girā
children.translated_text: For how many births have you not performed action with body, mind, and speech?

children.text: duḥkham āyāsadaṃ karma tad adyāpy uparamyatām ||
children.translated_text: That action, which brings suffering and exhaustion, should cease even today.

children.text: Chapter 11
aṣṭāvakra uvāca
children.translated_text: <s>Aṣṭāvakra</s> said:

children.text: bhāvābhāvavikāraś ca svabhāvād iti niścayī
children.translated_text: One who is certain that existence, nonexistence, and change occur by nature

children.text: nirvikāro gatakleśaḥ sukhenaivopaśāmyati ||
children.translated_text: becomes changeless, free from affliction, and easily comes to peace.

children.text: īśvaraḥ sarvanirmātā nehānya iti niścayī
children.translated_text: One who is certain that the Lord is the maker of all and that there is no other here

children.text: antargalitasarvāśaḥ śāntaḥ kvāpi na sajjate ||
children.translated_text: has all expectations melted away within; peaceful, he is attached nowhere at all.

children.text: āpadaḥ sampadaḥ kāle daivād eveti niścayī
children.translated_text: One who is certain that adversity and prosperity come in time by fate alone

children.text: tṛptaḥ svasthendriyo nityaṃ na vāñchati na śocati ||
children.translated_text: is content, with senses established in himself, and never desires or grieves.

children.text: sukhaduḥkhe janmamṛtyū daivād eveti niścayī
children.translated_text: One who is certain that pleasure and pain, birth and death, come by fate alone

children.text: sādhyādarśī nirāyāsaḥ kurvann api na lipyate ||
children.translated_text: sees nothing to be accomplished; effortless, even while acting, he is not tainted.

children.text: cintayā jāyate duḥkhaṃ nānyatheheti niścayī
children.translated_text: One who is certain that suffering arises from thought and not otherwise in this world

children.text: tayā hīnaḥ sukhī śāntaḥ sarvatra galitaspṛhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: is free from that thought, happy, peaceful, and everywhere devoid of longing.

children.text: nāhaṃ deho na me deho bodho 'ham iti niścayī
children.translated_text: One who is certain, 'I am not the body, nor is the body mine; I am awakening,'

children.text: kaivalyam iva samprāpto na smaraty akṛtaṃ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: as though having attained absolute aloneness, does not remember what has not been done or what has been done.

children.text: ā brahmastambaparyantam aham eveti niścayī
children.translated_text: One who is certain, 'From <s>Brahmā</s> down to a clump of grass, I alone am,'

children.text: nirvikalpaḥ śuciḥ śāntaḥ prāptāprāptavinirvṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: is free from conceptual division, pure, peaceful, and released from what is obtained and not obtained.

children.text: nānāścaryam idaṃ viśvaṃ na kiṃcid iti niścayī
children.translated_text: One who is certain, 'This universe of many wonders is nothing at all,'

children.text: nirvāsanaḥ sphūrtimātro na kiṃcid iva śāmyati ||
children.translated_text: free from vāsanās and consisting only of shining awareness, becomes peaceful, as if nothing at all.

children.text: Chapter 12
janaka uvāca
children.translated_text: <s>Janaka</s> said:

children.text: kāyakṛtyāsahaḥ pūrvaṃ tato vāgvistarāsahaḥ
children.translated_text: At first I could not endure bodily action; then I could not endure extensive speech;

children.text: atha cintāsahas tasmād evam evāham āsthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: after that I could not endure thought. Therefore I remain established just as I am.

children.text: prītyabhāvena śabdāder adṛśyatvena cātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Because there is no attachment to sound and the other sense objects, and because the self is not an object of sight,

children.text: vikṣepaikāgrahṛdaya evam evāhaṃ āsthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: my heart is beyond distraction and one-pointedness; therefore I remain established just as I am.

children.text: samādhyāsādivikṣiptau vyavahāraḥ samādhaye
children.translated_text: Practice beginning with samādhi is undertaken for the sake of samādhi when there is distraction.

children.text: evaṃ vilokya niyamam evam evāham āsthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Seeing this rule in this way, I remain established just as I am.

children.text: heyopādeyavirahād evaṃ harṣaviṣādayoḥ
children.translated_text: Because rejection and acceptance are absent, and because in this way joy and sorrow

children.text: abhāvād adya he brahmann evam evāham āsthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: are absent today, O <s>brahman</s>, I remain established just as I am.

children.text: āśramānāśramaṃ dhyānaṃ cittasvīkṛtavarjanam
children.translated_text: Life-stage and no life-stage, meditation, the mind's acceptance and rejection:

children.text: vikalpaṃ mama vīkṣyaitair evam evāham āsthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: seeing that these are conceptual constructions for me, I remain established just as I am.

children.text: karmānuṣṭhānam ajñānād yathaivoparamas tathā
children.translated_text: The performance of action is indeed from ignorance, and so too is withdrawal.

children.text: buddhvā samyag idaṃ tattvam evam evāham āsthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having correctly understood this reality, I abide just so.

children.text: acintyaṃ cintyamāno 'pi cintārūpaṃ bhajaty asau
children.translated_text: Even when the unthinkable is thought about, it takes on the form of thought.

children.text: tyaktvā tadbhāvanaṃ tasmād evam evāham āsthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, abandoning the contemplation of that state, I abide just so.

children.text: evam eva kṛtaṃ yena sa kṛtārtho bhaved asau
children.translated_text: One by whom this very thing has been done becomes one whose purpose is fulfilled.

children.text: evam eva svabhāvo yaḥ sa kṛtārtho bhaved asau ||
children.translated_text: One whose very nature is just so becomes one whose purpose is fulfilled.

children.text: Chapter 13
janaka uvāca
children.translated_text: <s>Janaka</s> said:

children.text: akiṃcanabhavaṃ svāsthyaṃ kaupīnatve 'pi durlabham
children.translated_text: The well-being born of possessing nothing is hard to attain even when one has only a loincloth.

children.text: tyāgādāne vihāyāsmād aham āse yathāsukham ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, abandoning both renunciation and acquisition, I sit at ease as I please.

children.text: kutrāpi khedaḥ kāyasya jihvā kutrāpi khidyate
children.translated_text: Somewhere there is weariness of the body; somewhere the tongue grows weary.

children.text: manaḥ kutrāpi tat tyaktvā puruṣārthe sthitaḥ sukham ||
children.translated_text: Somewhere the mind grows weary. Having abandoned that, I stand happily in the true aim of a person.

children.text: kṛtaṃ kim api naiva syād iti saṃcintya tattvataḥ
children.translated_text: Considering truly that nothing at all has really been done,

children.text: yadā yat kartum āyāti tat kṛtvāse yathāsukham ||
children.translated_text: whenever something comes to be done, I do it and remain at ease as I please.

children.text: karmanaiṣkarmyanirbandhabhāvā dehasthayoginaḥ
children.translated_text: The notions of insistence on action and non-action belong to yogins who identify with the body.

children.text: saṃyogāyogavirahād aham āse yathāsukham ||
children.translated_text: Because I am free from conjunction and disjunction, I remain at ease as I please.

children.text: arthānarthau na me sthityā gatyā na śayanena vā
children.translated_text: For me there is no gain or loss by standing, by going, or by lying down.

children.text: tiṣṭhan gacchan svapan tasmād aham āse yathāsukham ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, standing, going, or sleeping, I remain at ease as I please.

children.text: svapato nāsti me hāniḥ siddhir yatnavato na vā
children.translated_text: There is no loss for me when I sleep, nor any success when I exert myself.

children.text: nāśollāsau vihāyāsmād aham āse yathāsukham ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, abandoning destruction and elation, I remain at ease as I please.

children.text: sukhādirūpā niyamaṃ bhāveṣv ālokya bhūriśaḥ
children.translated_text: Having repeatedly observed that conditions such as pleasure are regular among experiences,

children.text: śubhāśubhe vihāyāsmād aham āse yathāsukham ||
children.translated_text: therefore, abandoning good and bad, I remain at ease as I please.

children.text: Chapter 14
janaka uvāca
children.translated_text: <s>Janaka</s> said:

children.text: prakṛtyā śūnyacitto yaḥ pramādād bhāvabhāvanaḥ
children.translated_text: One whose mind is by nature empty, though through heedlessness he imagines states,

children.text: nidrito bodhita iva kṣīṇasaṃsmaraṇo hi saḥ ||
children.translated_text: is like one awakened from sleep; indeed, his recollection has faded away.

children.text: kva dhanāni kva mitrāṇi kva me viṣayadasyavaḥ
children.translated_text: Where are riches? Where are friends? Where are the thieves called sense-objects for me?

children.text: kva śāstraṃ kva ca vijñānaṃ yadā me galitā spṛhā ||
children.translated_text: Where is scripture, and where is knowledge, when longing has fallen away from me?

children.text: vijñāte sākṣipuruṣe paramātmani ceśvare
children.translated_text: When the witness-person, the supreme self and Lord, has been known,

children.text: nairāśye bandhamokṣe ca na cintā muktaye mama ||
children.translated_text: and when hope regarding bondage and liberation is gone, I have no concern for liberation.

children.text: antarvikalpaśūnyasya bahiḥ svacchandacāriṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Of one who is empty of inner alternatives and wanders freely outside,

children.text: bhrāntasyeva daśās tās tās tādṛśā eva jānate ||
children.translated_text: his various states, as if those of a deluded man, are known only by those like him.

children.text: Chapter 15
aṣṭāvakra uvāca
children.translated_text: <s>Aṣṭāvakra</s> said:

children.text: yathātathopadeśena kṛtārthaḥ sattvabuddhimān
children.translated_text: A person of pure understanding, fulfilled by instruction of whatever kind,

children.text: ājīvam api jijñāsuḥ paras tatra vimuhyati ||
children.translated_text: is different; one who remains a seeker even for life is bewildered there.

children.text: mokṣo viṣayavairasyaṃ bandho vaiṣayiko rasaḥ
children.translated_text: Liberation is dispassion toward sense-objects; bondage is relish for sense-objects.

children.text: etāvad eva vijñānaṃ yathecchasi tathā kuru ||
children.translated_text: Knowledge is only this much. Do as you wish.

children.text: vāgmiprājñamahodyogaṃ janaṃ mūkajaḍālasam
children.translated_text: This awakening to reality makes a person eloquent, wise, and greatly energetic become silent, dull, and lazy.

children.text: karoti tattvabodho 'yam atas tyakto bubhukṣubhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: For that reason it is shunned by those who desire enjoyment.

children.text: na tvaṃ deho na te deho bhoktā kartā na vā bhavān
children.translated_text: You are not the body, nor is the body yours; you are neither enjoyer nor agent.

children.text: cidrūpo 'si sadā sākṣī nirapekṣaḥ sukhaṃ cara ||
children.translated_text: You are of the nature of consciousness, always the witness; independent, move happily.

children.text: rāgadveṣau manodharmau na manas te kadācana
children.translated_text: Attachment and aversion are properties of the mind, and the mind is never yours.

children.text: nirvikalpo 'si bodhātmā nirvikāraḥ sukhaṃ cara ||
children.translated_text: You are free from conceptual alternatives, the self whose nature is awakening, changeless; move happily.

children.text: sarvabhūteṣu cātmānaṃ sarvabhūtāni cātmani
children.translated_text: Having known the self in all beings and all beings in the self,

children.text: vijñāya nirahaṃkāro nirmamas tvaṃ sukhī bhava ||
children.translated_text: be free from ego and free from possessiveness, and be happy.

children.text: viśvaṃ sphurati yatredaṃ taraṅgā iva sāgare
children.translated_text: That in which this universe shines forth like waves in the ocean,

children.text: tat tvam eva na sandehaś cinmūrte vijvaro bhava ||
children.translated_text: that is you alone, without doubt; O embodiment of consciousness, be free from fever.

children.text: śraddhatsva tāta śraddhatsva nātra mohaṃ kuruṣva bhoḥ
children.translated_text: Have faith, dear one, have faith; do not fall into delusion here, sir.

children.text: jñānasvarūpo bhagavān ātmā tvaṃ prakṛteḥ paraḥ ||
children.translated_text: You are the blessed self, whose nature is knowledge, beyond <s>prakṛti</s> (primordial nature).

children.text: guṇaiḥ saṃveṣṭito dehas tiṣṭhaty āyāti yāti ca
children.translated_text: The body, enveloped by the guṇas, stands, comes, and goes.

children.text: ātmā na gantā nāgantā kim enam anuśocasi ||
children.translated_text: The self neither goes nor comes. Why do you grieve over it?

children.text: dehas tiṣṭhatu kalpāntaṃ gacchatv adyaiva vā punaḥ
children.translated_text: Let the body remain until the end of the aeon, or let it go this very day again.

children.text: kva vṛddhiḥ kva ca vā hānis tava cinmātrarūpiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What increase or what loss is there for you, whose form is mere consciousness?

children.text: tvayy anantamahāmbhodhau viśvavīciḥ svabhāvataḥ
children.translated_text: In you, the infinite great ocean, the wave of the universe, by its own nature,

children.text: udetu vāstam āyātu na te vṛddhir na vā kṣatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: may arise or set; there is no increase or injury for you.

children.text: tāta cinmātrarūpo 'si na te bhinnam idaṃ jagat
children.translated_text: Dear one, you are of the form of mere consciousness; this world is not separate from you.

children.text: ataḥ kasya kathaṃ kutra heyopādeyakalpanā ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, for whom, how, and where can there be the imagining of what is to be rejected or accepted?

children.text: ekasminn avyaye śānte cidākāśe 'male tvayi
children.translated_text: In you, the one, imperishable, peaceful, stainless space of consciousness,

children.text: kuto janma kutaḥ karma kuto 'haṃkāra eva ca ||
children.translated_text: whence could there be birth, whence action, and whence even ego?

children.text: yat tvaṃ paśyasi tatraikas tvam eva pratibhāsase
children.translated_text: Wherever you see, you alone appear as the one there.

children.text: kiṃ pṛthak bhāsate svarṇāt kaṭakāṅgadanūpuram ||
children.translated_text: Does a bracelet, armlet, or anklet appear as something separate from gold?

children.text: ayaṃ so 'ham ayam nāhaṃ vibhāgam iti saṃtyaja
children.translated_text: Abandon the division, 'This is I; that I am not.'

children.text: sarvam ātmeti niścitya niḥsaṃkalpaḥ sukhī bhava ||
children.translated_text: Having determined that all is the self, be free of intentions and be happy.

children.text: tavaivājñānato viśvaṃ tvam ekaḥ paramārthataḥ
children.translated_text: The universe exists through your ignorance alone; in the highest truth you are one.

children.text: tvatto 'nyo nāsti saṃsārī nāsaṃsārī ca kaścana ||
children.translated_text: There is no one other than you, neither bound in saṃsāra nor free from saṃsāra.

children.text: bhrāntimātram idaṃ viśvaṃ na kiṃcid iti niścayī
children.translated_text: This universe is mere delusion; one who is certain that it is nothing at all,

children.text: nirvāsanaḥ sphūrtimātro na kiṃcid iva śāmyati ||
children.translated_text: free from latent desires and mere manifestation, becomes peaceful as if nothing at all.

children.text: eka eva bhavāmbhodhāv āsīd asti bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: In the ocean of becoming, the one alone was, is, and will be.

children.text: na te bandho 'sti mokṣo vā kṛtakṛtyaḥ sukhaṃ cara ||
children.translated_text: For you there is neither bondage nor liberation; with your task accomplished, move happily.

children.text: mā saṅkalpavikalpābhyāṃ cittaṃ kṣobhaya cinmaya
children.translated_text: O one made of consciousness, do not disturb the mind with intention and counter-intention.

children.text: upaśāmya sukhaṃ tiṣṭha svātmany ānandavigrahe ||
children.translated_text: Become quiet and remain happily in your own self, whose form is bliss.

children.text: tyajaiva dhyānaṃ sarvatra mā kiṃciddhṛdi dhāraya
children.translated_text: Abandon meditation altogether; do not hold anything in the heart.

children.text: ātmā tvaṃ mukta evāsi kiṃ vimṛśya kariṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: You are the self and are already free. What will you do by deliberating?

children.text: Chapter 16
aṣṭāvakra uvāca
children.translated_text: <s>Aṣṭāvakra</s> said:

children.text: ācakṣva śṛṇu vā tāta nānāśāstrāṇyanekaśaḥ
children.translated_text: Explain or listen, dear one, to many scriptures again and again;

children.text: tathāpi na tava svāsthyaṃ sarvavismaraṇād ṛte ||
children.translated_text: even so, well-being is not yours except through forgetting everything.

children.text: bhogaṃ karma samādhiṃ vā kuru vijña tathāpi te
children.translated_text: Practice enjoyment, action, or <s>samādhi</s> (absorption), O wise one; even so, your

children.text: cittaṃ nirastasarvāśam atyarthaṃ rocayiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: mind, from which all hope has been cast out, will be exceedingly pleased.

children.text: āyāsāt sakalo duḥkhī nainaṃ jānāti kaścana
children.translated_text: Everyone is miserable because of exertion, but no one knows this.

children.text: anenaivopadeśena dhanyaḥ prāpnoti nirvṛtim ||
children.translated_text: By this instruction alone, the blessed one attains repose.

children.text: vyāpāre khidyate yas tu nimeṣonmeṣayor api
children.translated_text: But one who is wearied by activity even in the closing and opening of the eyes

children.text: tasyālasyadhurīṇasya sukhaṃ nānyasya kasyacit ||
children.translated_text: Happiness belongs to that foremost idler, and to no one else.

children.text: idaṃ kṛtam idaṃ neti dvandvair muktaṃ yadā manaḥ
children.translated_text: When the mind is freed from pairs of opposites such as 'this has been done' and 'this has not,'

children.text: dharmārthakāmamokṣeṣu nirapekṣaṃ tadā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: then it becomes without expectation regarding <s>dharma</s>, wealth, desire, and liberation.

children.text: virakto viṣayadveṣṭā rāgī viṣayalolupaḥ
children.translated_text: One who is detached hates sense objects; one who is attached is greedy for sense objects.

children.text: grahamokṣavihīnas tu na virakto na rāgavān ||
children.translated_text: But one who is free from grasping and release is neither detached nor attached.

children.text: heyopādeyatā tāvat saṃsāraviṭapāṅkuraḥ
children.translated_text: So long as the desire to reject and accept remains alive, it is the sprout of the tree of saṃsāra,

children.text: spṛhā jīvati yāvad vai nirvicāradaśāspadam ||
children.translated_text: the seat of the state without discrimination.

children.text: pravṛttau jāyate rāgo nirvṛttau dveṣa eva hi
children.translated_text: Attachment arises in activity, and aversion indeed in withdrawal.

children.text: nirdvandvo bālavad dhīmān evam eva vyavasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus the wise person, free from duality, remains just like a child.

children.text: hātum icchati saṃsāraṃ rāgī duḥkhajihāsayā
children.translated_text: The attached person wishes to abandon saṃsāra out of a desire to avoid suffering.

children.text: vītarāgo hi nirduḥkhas tasminn api na khidyati ||
children.translated_text: But one whose attachment has departed is free from suffering and is not distressed even in it.

children.text: yasyābhimāno mokṣe 'pi dehe 'pi mamatā tathā
children.translated_text: One who has pride even in liberation, and likewise possessiveness toward the body,

children.text: na ca jñānī na vā yogī kevalaṃ duḥkhabhāg asau ||
children.translated_text: is neither a knower nor a yogin; he is merely a sharer in suffering.

children.text: haro yady upadeṣṭā te hariḥ kamalajo 'pi vā
children.translated_text: Even if <s>Hara</s> were your instructor, or <s>Hari</s>, or even the lotus-born <s>Brahmā</s>,

children.text: tathāpi na tava svāsthyaṃ sarvavismaraṇād ṛte ||
children.translated_text: still you would have no inner well-being except through forgetting everything.

children.text: Chapter 17
aṣṭāvakra uvāca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Aṣṭāvakra</s> said:

children.text: tena jñānaphalaṃ prāptaṃ yogābhyāsaphalaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: He has obtained the fruit of knowledge, and likewise the fruit of the practice of yoga,

children.text: tṛptaḥ svacchendriyo nityam ekākī ramate tu yaḥ ||
children.translated_text: who, satisfied, with clear senses, always delights alone.

children.text: na kadācij jagaty asmiṃs tattvajño hanta khidyati
children.translated_text: The knower of reality is never, alas, distressed in this world,

children.text: yata ekena tenedaṃ pūrṇaṃ brahmāṇḍamaṇḍalam ||
children.translated_text: because this whole orb of the universe has been filled by that one alone.

children.text: na jātu viṣayāḥ ke'pi svārāmaṃ harṣayanty amī
children.translated_text: No sense objects whatsoever gladden one who delights in himself,

children.text: sallakīpallavaprītam ivebhaṃ nimbapallavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: just as neem leaves do not gladden an elephant pleased with sallakī leaves.

children.text: yas tu bhogeṣu bhukteṣu na bhavaty adhivāsitaḥ
children.translated_text: But one who is not perfumed by enjoyments already enjoyed,

children.text: abhukteṣu nirākāṅkṣī tādṛśo bhavadurlabhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and who has no longing for those not enjoyed, such a person is hard to find in existence.

children.text: bubhukṣur iha saṃsāre mumukṣur api dṛśyate
children.translated_text: In this saṃsāra one sees both one who longs to enjoy and one who longs for liberation.

children.text: bhogamokṣanirākāṅkṣī viralo hi mahāśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But rare indeed is the great-souled one who has no longing for either enjoyment or liberation.

children.text: dharmārthakāmamokṣeṣu jīvite maraṇe tathā
children.translated_text: With regard to <s>dharma</s>, wealth, desire, liberation, and likewise life and death,

children.text: kasyāpy udāracittasya heyopādeyatā na hi ||
children.translated_text: for some noble-minded person there is no thought of what is to be rejected or accepted.

children.text: vāñchā na viśvavilaye na dveṣas tasya ca sthitau
children.translated_text: He has no wish for the dissolution of the universe, nor any hatred of its continuance.

children.text: yathā jīvikayā tasmād dhanya āste yathāsukhaṃ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, living as life comes, that blessed one abides at ease.

children.text: kṛtārtho 'nena jñānenety evaṃ galitadhīḥ kṛtī
children.translated_text: Thinking, 'I have accomplished my purpose through this knowledge,' his thought dissolved, fulfilled,

children.text: paśyan śṛṇvan spṛśan jighrann aśnann āste yathāsukhaṃ ||
children.translated_text: he abides at ease, seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, and eating.

children.text: śūnyā dṛṣṭir vṛthā ceṣṭā vikalānīndriyāṇi ca
children.translated_text: His gaze is empty, his activity purposeless, and his senses impaired;

children.text: na spṛhā na viraktir vā kṣīṇasaṃsārasāgare ||
children.translated_text: there is neither craving nor detachment for one whose ocean of saṃsāra has been exhausted.

children.text: na jāgarti na nidrāti nonmīlati na mīlati
children.translated_text: He does not wake, does not sleep, does not open his eyes, and does not close them.

children.text: aho paradaśā kvāpi vartate muktacetasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Ah! Somewhere the supreme state of one whose mind is liberated exists.

children.text: sarvatra dṛśyate svasthaḥ sarvatra vimalāśayaḥ
children.translated_text: Everywhere he is seen as self-abiding; everywhere his intention is stainless.

children.text: samastavāsanāmukto muktaḥ sarvatra rājate ||
children.translated_text: Free from all latent tendencies, the liberated one shines everywhere.

children.text: paśyan śṛṇvan spṛśan jighrann aśnan gṛhṇan vadanvrajan
children.translated_text: Seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, taking, speaking, and walking,

children.text: īhitānīhitair mukto mukta eva mahāśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: free from what is desired and not desired, the great-souled one is liberated indeed.

children.text: na nindati na ca stauti na hṛṣyati na kupyati
children.translated_text: He does not blame and does not praise; he does not rejoice and does not become angry.

children.text: na dadāti na gṛhṇāti muktaḥ sarvatra nīrasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He does not give and does not take; the liberated one is everywhere devoid of relish.

children.text: sānurāgāṃ striyaṃ dṛṣṭvā mṛtyuṃ vā samupasthitam
children.translated_text: Seeing a passionate woman, or death standing before him,

children.text: avihvalamanāḥ svastho mukta eva mahāśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: with mind unagitated and self-possessed, the great-souled one is liberated indeed.

children.text: sukhe duḥkhe nare nāryāṃ sampatsu ca vipatsu ca
children.translated_text: In happiness and suffering, in a man or a woman, in prosperity and adversity,

children.text: viśeṣo naiva dhīrasya sarvatra samadarśinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: there is no distinction at all for the steadfast one who sees equally everywhere.

children.text: na hiṃsā naiva kāruṇyaṃ nauddhatyaṃ na ca dīnatā
children.translated_text: There is no violence, no compassion, no arrogance, and no humility;

children.text: nāścaryaṃ naiva ca kṣobhaḥ kṣīṇasaṃsaraṇe nare ||
children.translated_text: there is no wonder and no agitation in the person whose wandering through saṃsāra has been exhausted.

children.text: na mukto viṣayadveṣṭā na vā viṣayalolupaḥ
children.translated_text: The liberated one is not a hater of sense objects, nor is he greedy for sense objects.

children.text: asaṃsaktamanā nityaṃ prāptāprāptam upāśnute ||
children.translated_text: With mind always unattached, he enjoys what has come and what has not come.

children.text: samādhānāsamādhānahitāhitavikalpanāḥ
children.translated_text: Conceptual distinctions about concentration and non-concentration, benefit and harm,

children.text: śūnyacitto na jānāti kaivalyam iva saṃsthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the one whose mind is empty does not know, standing as if in absolute isolation.

children.text: nirmamo nirahaṃkāro na kiṃcid iti niścitaḥ
children.translated_text: Free from 'mine' and free from ego, certain that nothing exists,

children.text: antargalitasarvāśaḥ kurvann api karoti na ||
children.translated_text: with every hope inwardly dissolved, even acting, he does not act.

children.text: manaḥprakāśasammohasvapnajāḍyavivarjitaḥ
children.translated_text: Devoid of illumination and delusion of mind, dream, and dullness,

children.text: daśāṃ kāmapi samprāpto bhaved galitamānasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: one whose mind has dissolved may reach some indescribable state.

children.text: Chapter 18
aṣṭāvakra uvāca
children.translated_text: <s>Aṣṭāvakra</s> said:

children.text: yasya bodhodaye tāvat svapnavad bhavati bhramaḥ
children.translated_text: For the one at whose arising of awakening delusion immediately becomes like a dream,

children.text: tasmai sukhaikarūpāya namaḥ śāntāya tejase ||
children.translated_text: homage to that peaceful radiance whose sole form is happiness.

children.text: arjayitvākhilān arthān bhogān āpnoti puṣkalān
children.translated_text: Having acquired all objects, one obtains abundant enjoyments,

children.text: na hi sarvaparityāgam antareṇa sukhī bhavet ||
children.translated_text: yet one cannot be happy without complete renunciation.

children.text: kartavyaduḥkhamārtaṇḍajvālād agdhāntarātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: For one whose inner self is scorched by the flames of the sun of duty's suffering,

children.text: kutaḥ praśamapīyūṣadhārāsāram ṛte sukham ||
children.translated_text: how can there be happiness without the stream of the nectar of tranquility?

children.text: bhavo 'yaṃ bhāvanāmātro na kiṃcit paramārthataḥ
children.translated_text: This becoming is mere imagination; ultimately it is nothing.

children.text: nāsty abhāvaḥ svabhāvānāṃ bhāvābhāvavibhāvinām ||
children.translated_text: There is no nonexistence of things whose nature is to manifest existence and nonexistence.

children.text: na dūraṃ na ca saṅkocāl labdham evātmanaḥ padam
children.translated_text: The state of the self is not far away, nor is it obtained by contraction;

children.text: nirvikalpaṃ nirāyāsaṃ nirvikāraṃ nirañjanam ||
children.translated_text: it is nonconceptual, effortless, unchanging, and stainless.

children.text: vyāmohamātraviratau svarūpādānamātrataḥ
children.translated_text: Through the mere cessation of bewilderment, through the mere taking up of one's own nature,

children.text: vītaśokā virājante nirāvaraṇadṛṣṭayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: those whose vision is unobstructed shine, free from sorrow.

children.text: samastaṃ kalpanāmātram ātmā muktaḥ sanātanaḥ
children.translated_text: Everything is merely imagination; the self is free and eternal.

children.text: iti vijñāya dhīro hi kim abhyasyati bālavat ||
children.translated_text: Knowing this, why should the steadfast person practice like a child?

children.text: ātmā brahmeti niścitya bhāvābhāvau ca kalpitau
children.translated_text: Having ascertained, 'The self is brahman,' and that existence and nonexistence are imagined,

children.text: niṣkāmaḥ kiṃ vijānāti kiṃ brūte ca karoti kiṃ ||
children.translated_text: what does the desireless one know, what does he say, and what does he do?

children.text: ayaṃ so 'ham ayaṃ nāham iti kṣīṇā vikalpanāḥ
children.translated_text: For the yogin who has become silent, having ascertained that everything is the self,

children.text: sarvam ātmeti niścitya tuṣṇībhūtasya yoginaḥ ||
children.translated_text: conceptions such as 'this is I' and 'this is not I' have been exhausted.

children.text: na vikṣepo na caikāgryaṃ nātibodho na mūḍhatā
children.translated_text: There is no distraction and no one-pointedness, no excessive knowledge and no dullness,

children.text: na sukhaṃ na ca vā duḥkham upaśāntasya yoginaḥ ||
children.translated_text: no happiness and no suffering for the pacified yogin.

children.text: svārājye bhaikṣavṛttau ca lābhālābhe jane vane
children.translated_text: In sovereignty and in a mendicant's livelihood, in gain and loss, among people and in the forest...

children.text: nirvikalpasvabhāvasya na viśeṣo 'sti yoginaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the yogin whose nature is free from conceptual alternatives, there is no distinction.

children.text: kva dharmaḥ kva ca vā kāmaḥ kva cārthaḥ kva vivekitā
children.translated_text: Where is <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), where indeed is desire, where is wealth, and where is discrimination

children.text: idaṃ kṛtam idaṃ neti dvandvair muktasya yoginaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for the yogin who is freed from the pairs of opposites, 'this has been done' and 'this has not'?

children.text: kṛtyaṃ kim api naivāsti na kāpi hṛdi rañjanā
children.translated_text: There is no duty at all to be done, nor any delight in the heart

children.text: yathājīvanam eveha jīvanmuktasya yoginaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for the yogin liberated while living here, who lives just according to life as it comes.

children.text: kva mohaḥ kva ca vā viśvaṃ kva tad dhyānaṃ kva muktatā
children.translated_text: Where is delusion, where indeed is the universe, where is that meditation, and where is liberation

children.text: sarvasaṅkalpasīmāyāṃ viśrāntasya mahātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for the great-souled one who has rested at the limit of all conceptual intentions?

children.text: yena viśvam idaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ sa nāstīti karotu vai
children.translated_text: Let the one by whom this universe has been seen declare, if he wishes, that it does not exist.

children.text: nirvāsanaḥ kiṃ kurute paśyann api na paśyati ||
children.translated_text: What does the desireless one do? Though seeing, he does not see.

children.text: yena dṛṣṭaṃ paraṃ brahma so 'haṃ brahmeti cintayet
children.translated_text: The one by whom supreme <s>brahman</s> has been seen may think, 'I am <s>brahman</s>.'

children.text: kiṃ cintayati niścinto dvitīyaṃ yo na paśyati ||
children.translated_text: What does the thought-free one think, who sees no second thing?

children.text: dṛṣṭo yenātmavikṣepo nirodhaṃ kurute tv asau
children.translated_text: The one by whom the disturbance of the self has been seen undertakes its restraint.

children.text: udāras tu na vikṣiptaḥ sādhyābhāvāt karoti kim ||
children.translated_text: But the noble one is not disturbed; since there is nothing to be accomplished, what does he do?

children.text: dhīro lokaviparyasto vartamāno 'pi lokavat
children.translated_text: The steadfast one, different from the world, though behaving like the world,

children.text: na samādhiṃ na vikṣepaṃ na lepaṃ svasya paśyati ||
children.translated_text: sees neither samādhi, nor distraction, nor any stain as his own.

children.text: bhāvābhāvavihīno yas tṛpto nirvāsano budhaḥ
children.translated_text: The wise one who is free from being and non-being, satisfied, and desireless,

children.text: naiva kiṃcit kṛtaṃ tena lokadṛṣṭyā vikurvatā ||
children.translated_text: has done nothing at all, though from the world's viewpoint he acts in various ways.

children.text: pravṛttau vā nirvṛttau vā naiva dhīrasya durgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: Whether in activity or withdrawal, there is no obstinate grasping for the steadfast one,

children.text: yadā yat kartum āyāti tatkṛtvā tiṣṭhataḥ sukham ||
children.translated_text: who remains happy after doing whatever comes to be done at any time.

children.text: nirvāsano nirālambaḥ svacchando muktabandhanaḥ
children.translated_text: Desireless, unsupported, moving by his own will, released from bondage,

children.text: kṣiptaḥ saṃskāravātena ceṣṭate śuṣkaparṇavat ||
children.translated_text: he acts when cast about by the wind of impressions, like a dry leaf.

children.text: asaṃsārasya tu kvāpi na harṣo na viṣāditā
children.translated_text: For one who is beyond saṃsāra, nowhere is there elation and nowhere despondency.

children.text: sa śītalamanā nityaṃ videha iva rājate ||
children.translated_text: With a cool mind, he always shines like one bodiless.

children.text: kutrāpi na jihāsāsti nāśo vāpi na kutracit
children.translated_text: Nowhere does he have any wish to abandon anything, nor is there loss anywhere

children.text: ātmārāmasya dhīrasya śītalācchatarātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for the steadfast one who delights in the self, whose inner self is cool and clear.

children.text: prakṛtyā śūnyacittasya kurvato 'sya yadṛcchayā
children.translated_text: For this steadfast one, whose mind is naturally empty and who acts by chance,

children.text: prākṛtasyeva dhīrasya na māno nāvamānatā ||
children.translated_text: there is no honor and no dishonor, as if he were an ordinary man.

children.text: kṛtaṃ dehena karmedaṃ na mayā śuddharūpiṇā
children.translated_text: 'This action has been done by the body, not by me, whose form is pure':

children.text: iti cintānurodhī yaḥ kurvann api karoti na ||
children.translated_text: one who acts in accordance with this reflection, even while acting, does not act.

children.text: atadvādīva kurute na bhaved api bāliśaḥ
children.translated_text: He acts as if speaking otherwise, yet he is not childish.

children.text: jīvanmuktaḥ sukhī śrīmān saṃsarann api śobhate ||
children.translated_text: The happy and fortunate liberated-while-living one shines even while moving through the world.

children.text: nānāvicārasuśrānto dhīro viśrāntim āgataḥ
children.translated_text: The steadfast one, well wearied by many reflections, has come to rest.

children.text: na kalpate na jānāti na śṛṇoti na paśyati ||
children.translated_text: He does not imagine, does not know, does not hear, and does not see.

children.text: asamādher avikṣepān na mumukṣur na cetaraḥ
children.translated_text: Because there is no non-samādhi and no distraction, he is neither a seeker of liberation nor the opposite.

children.text: niścitya kalpitaṃ paśyan brahmaivāste mahāśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Seeing what is imagined after certainty, the great-hearted one abides as <s>brahman</s> alone.

children.text: yasyāntaḥ syād ahaṅkāro na karoti karoti saḥ
children.translated_text: He in whom there is ego inside acts even when he does not act.

children.text: nirahaṅkāradhīreṇa na kiṃcid akṛtaṃ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: By the steadfast one free from ego, nothing undone or done has been made.

children.text: nodvignaṃ na ca saṃtuṣṭam akartṛ spandavarjitam
children.translated_text: Not agitated, not satisfied, non-doing, devoid of movement,

children.text: nirāśaṃ gatasandehaṃ cittaṃ muktasya rājate ||
children.translated_text: free from expectation and rid of doubt, the mind of the liberated one shines.

children.text: nirdhyātuṃ ceṣṭituṃ vāpi yac cittaṃ na pravartate
children.translated_text: The mind that does not set out either to meditate or to act

children.text: nirnimittam idaṃ kiṃ tu nirdhyāyati viceṣṭate ||
children.translated_text: nevertheless meditates and acts, but without a motive.

children.text: tattvaṃ yathārtham ākarṇya mandaḥ prāpnoti mūḍhatām
children.translated_text: Having heard reality just as it is, the dull person falls into confusion,

children.text: atha vāyāti saṅkocam amūḍhaḥ ko 'pi mūḍhavat ||
children.translated_text: or else he contracts inwardly; some undeluded person may appear like a fool.

children.text: ekāgratā nirodho vā mūḍhair abhyasyate bhṛśam
children.translated_text: Concentration or restraint is practiced intensely by the dull.

children.text: dhīrāḥ kṛtyaṃ na paśyanti suptavat svapade sthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The steadfast do not see anything to be done; established in their own state, they are like sleepers.

children.text: aprayatnāt prayatnād vā mūḍho nāpnoti nirvṛtim
children.translated_text: The dull person does not attain cessation either without effort or with effort.

children.text: tattvaniścayamātreṇa prājño bhavati nirvṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By the mere certainty of reality, the wise person becomes fulfilled and at rest.

children.text: śuddhaṃ buddhaṃ priyaṃ pūrṇaṃ niṣprapañcaṃ nirāmayam
children.translated_text: Pure, awakened, beloved, complete, free from manifestation, and free from illness:

children.text: ātmānaṃ taṃ na jānanti tatrābhyāsaparā janāḥ ||
children.translated_text: people devoted to practice do not know that self.

children.text: nāpnoti karmaṇā mokṣaṃ vimūḍho 'bhyāsarūpiṇā
children.translated_text: The bewildered person does not attain liberation by action in the form of practice.

children.text: dhanyo vijñānamātreṇa muktas tiṣṭhaty avikriyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The fortunate one, by knowledge alone, remains liberated and unchanged.

children.text: mūḍho nāpnoti tad brahma yato bhavitum icchati
children.translated_text: The fool does not attain that <s>brahman</s>, because he wishes to become it.

children.text: anicchann api dhīro hi parabrahmasvarūpabhāk ||
children.translated_text: But the steadfast one, even without wishing, partakes of the nature of supreme <s>brahman</s>.

children.text: nirādhārā grahavyagrā mūḍhāḥ saṃsārapoṣakāḥ
children.translated_text: The foolish, without support and busied with grasping, nourish saṃsāra.

children.text: etasyānarthamūlasya mūlacchedaḥ kṛto budhaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The wise have cut the root of this source of misfortune.

children.text: na śāntiṃ labhate mūḍho yataḥ śamitum icchati
children.translated_text: The fool does not attain peace, because he wishes to make himself pacified.

children.text: dhīras tattvaṃ viniścitya sarvadā śāntamānasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The steadfast one, having ascertained reality, is always peaceful in mind.

children.text: kvātmano darśanaṃ tasya yad dṛṣṭam avalambate
children.translated_text: How can there be vision of the self for one who relies on what is seen?

children.text: dhīrās taṃ taṃ na paśyanti paśyanty ātmānam avyayam ||
children.translated_text: The steadfast do not see this or that; they see the imperishable self.

children.text: kva nirodho vimūḍhasya yo nirbandhaṃ karoti vai
children.translated_text: How can there be restraint for the bewildered one who indeed imposes constraint?

children.text: svārāmasyaiva dhīrasya sarvadāsāv akṛtrimaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the steadfast one who delights in himself, that restraint is always natural.

children.text: bhāvasya bhāvakaḥ kaścin na kiṃcid bhāvako 'paraḥ
children.translated_text: Someone is an imaginer of being; another is not an imaginer of anything.

children.text: ubhayābhāvakaḥ kaścid evam eva nirākulaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Someone is an imaginer of the absence of both; just so, he is free from agitation.

children.text: śuddham advayam ātmānaṃ bhāvayanti kubuddhayaḥ
children.translated_text: Those of poor understanding contemplate the self as pure and nondual,

children.text: na tu jānanti saṃmohād yāvajjīvam anirvṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: but through delusion they do not know it, and remain unfulfilled as long as they live.

children.text: mumukṣor buddhir ālambam antareṇa na vidyate
children.translated_text: The intellect of one who seeks liberation does not exist without a support.

children.text: nirālambaiva niṣkāmā buddhir muktasya sarvadā ||
children.translated_text: The intellect of the liberated one is always unsupported and desireless.

children.text: viṣayadvīpino vīkṣya cakitāḥ śaraṇārthinaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing the tigers of sense-objects, the frightened ones seeking refuge

children.text: viśanti jhaṭiti kroḍaṃ nirodhaikāgryasiddhaye ||
children.translated_text: quickly enter the cave for the attainment of restraint and one-pointedness.

children.text: nirvāsanaṃ hariṃ dṛṣṭvā tūṣṇīṃ viṣayadantinaḥ
children.translated_text: When the elephants of sense-objects see the desireless lion, they become silent.

children.text: palāyante na śaktās te sevante kṛtacāṭavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Unable to approach, they flee; or, made flattering, they serve him.

children.text: na muktikārikāṃ dhatte niḥśaṅko yuktamānasaḥ
children.translated_text: The one whose mind is disciplined and free from doubt does not take up a formula for liberation.

children.text: paśyañchṛṇvan spṛśañ jighrann aśnann āste yathāsukham ||
children.translated_text: Seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, and eating, he remains just as he pleases.

children.text: vastuśravaṇamātreṇa śuddhabuddhir nirākulaḥ
children.translated_text: By merely hearing the real thing, one whose understanding is pure and free from agitation

children.text: naivācāramanācāram audāsyaṃ vā prapaśyati ||
children.translated_text: does not at all perceive conduct, misconduct, or indifference.

children.text: yadā yat kartum āyāti tadā tatkurute ṛjuḥ
children.translated_text: When something comes to be done, then the upright one does just that;

children.text: śubhaṃ vāpy aśubhaṃ vāpi tasya ceṣṭā hi bālavat ||
children.translated_text: whether good or even bad, his activity is indeed like that of a child.

children.text: svātantryāt sukham āpnoti svātantryāl labhate param
children.translated_text: From freedom he obtains happiness; from freedom he attains the highest.

children.text: svātantryān nirvṛtiṃ gacchet svātantryāt paramaṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: From freedom he goes to repose; from freedom he reaches the supreme state.

children.text: akartṛtvam abhoktṛtvaṃ svātmano manyate yadā
children.translated_text: When he regards non-agency and non-enjoyership as belonging to his own self,

children.text: tadā kṣīṇā bhavanty eva samastāś cittavṛttayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then all the movements of the mind indeed become exhausted.

children.text: ucchṛṅkhalāpy akṛtikā sthitir dhīrasya rājate
children.translated_text: Even unrestrained and uncontrived, the state of the steadfast one shines;

children.text: na tu saspṛhacittasya śāntir mūḍhasya kṛtrimā ||
children.translated_text: but the artificial peace of the fool whose mind is full of longing does not.

children.text: vilasanti mahābhogair viśanti girigahvarān
children.translated_text: The steadfast, whose imaginations have been cast off, sport among great enjoyments and enter mountain caves;

children.text: nirastakalpanā dhīrā abaddhā muktabuddhayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: unbound, their understanding is free.

children.text: śrotriyaṃ devatāṃ tīrtham aṅganāṃ bhūpatiṃ priyam
children.translated_text: Having seen and honored a Vedic scholar, a deity, a sacred ford, a woman, a king, or a beloved one,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā sampūjya dhīrasya na kāpi hṛdi vāsanā ||
children.translated_text: there is no latent impression at all in the heart of the steadfast one.

children.text: bhṛtyaiḥ putraiḥ kalatraiś ca dauhitraiś cāpi gotrajaiḥ
children.translated_text: Though laughed at and reviled by servants, sons, wives, grandsons, and kinsmen,

children.text: vihasya dhikkṛto yogī na yāti vikṛtiṃ manāk ||
children.translated_text: the yogin does not undergo even the slightest alteration.

children.text: saṃtuṣṭo 'pi na saṃtuṣṭaḥ khinno 'pi na ca khidyate
children.translated_text: Even content, he is not content; even distressed, he is not distressed.

children.text: tasyāścaryadaśāṃ tāṃ tāṃ tādṛśā eva jānate ||
children.translated_text: Only such people as he know each of those wondrous states of his.

children.text: kartavyataiva saṃsāro na tāṃ paśyanti sūrayaḥ
children.translated_text: The very sense of something to be done is <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly bondage); the wise do not see it.

children.text: śūnyākārā nirākārā nirvikārā nirāmayāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They are of the form of emptiness, formless, changeless, and free from affliction.

children.text: akurvann api saṃkṣobhād vyagraḥ sarvatra mūḍhadhīḥ
children.translated_text: Even when not acting, the foolish-minded man is agitated everywhere by disturbance;

children.text: kurvann api tu kṛtyāni kuśalo hi nirākulaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but the skillful one, even while performing actions, is indeed untroubled.

children.text: sukham āste sukhaṃ śete sukham āyāti yāti ca
children.translated_text: With ease he sits, with ease he lies down, with ease he comes and goes;

children.text: sukhaṃ vakti sukhaṃ bhuṅkte vyavahāre 'pi śāntadhīḥ ||
children.translated_text: with ease he speaks, with ease he eats, and even in ordinary dealings his understanding is peaceful.

children.text: svabhāvād yasya naivārtir lokavad vyavahāriṇaḥ
children.translated_text: He who, by nature, has no distress while dealing with the world like other people

children.text: mahāhrada ivākṣobhyo gatakleśaḥ suśobhate ||
children.translated_text: shines beautifully, his afflictions gone, unshaken like a great lake.

children.text: nivṛttir api mūḍhasya pravṛttir upajāyate
children.translated_text: Even withdrawal becomes activity for the fool;
