children.text: pravṛttir api dhīrasya nivṛttiphalabhāginī ||
children.translated_text: even activity for the steadfast one shares in the fruit of withdrawal.

children.text: parigraheṣu vairāgyaṃ prāyo mūḍhasya dṛśyate
children.translated_text: Dispassion toward possessions is generally seen in the fool;

children.text: dehe vigalitāśasya kva rāgaḥ kva virāgatā ||
children.translated_text: but for one whose hope has fallen away from the body, where is passion and where is dispassion?

children.text: bhāvanābhāvanāsaktā dṛṣṭir mūḍhasya sarvadā
children.translated_text: The vision of the fool is always attached to mental cultivation and non-cultivation;

children.text: bhāvyabhāvanayā sā tu svasthasyādṛṣṭirūpiṇī ||
children.translated_text: but through the non-conceiving of what is to be conceived, that vision of the one established in himself has the nature of non-vision.

children.text: sarvārambheṣu niṣkāmo yaś cared bālavan muniḥ
children.translated_text: If a sage, desireless in all undertakings, should move about like a child,

children.text: na lepas tasya śuddhasya kriyamāṇe 'pi karmaṇi ||
children.translated_text: there is no stain for that pure one, even when action is being performed.

children.text: sa eva dhanya ātmajñaḥ sarvabhāveṣu yaḥ samaḥ
children.translated_text: Blessed indeed is that knower of the self who is equal toward all states,

children.text: paśyan śṛṇvan spṛśan jighrann aśnan nistarṣamānasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, and eating, with a mind free from thirst.

children.text: kva saṃsāraḥ kva cābhāsaḥ kva sādhyaṃ kva ca sādhanam
children.translated_text: Where is <s>saṃsāra</s>, where appearance, where what is to be accomplished, and where the means to accomplish it,

children.text: ākāśasyeva dhīrasya nirvikalpasya sarvadā ||
children.translated_text: for the steadfast one, who is like space and always free from conceptual division?

children.text: sa jayaty arthasaṃnyāsī pūrṇasvarasavigrahaḥ
children.translated_text: He is victorious, the renouncer of aims, whose form is the fullness of his own essence,

children.text: akṛtrimo 'navacchinne samādhir yasya vartate ||
children.translated_text: and whose <s>samādhi</s> (absorption), uncontrived and unlimited, is present.

children.text: bahunātra kim uktena jñātatattvo mahāśayaḥ
children.translated_text: What more need be said here? The great-hearted one who has known reality,

children.text: bhogamokṣanirākāṅkṣī sadā sarvatra nīrasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: free from longing for enjoyment or liberation, is always and everywhere without relish.

children.text: mahadādi jagaddvaitaṃ nāmamātravijṛmbhitam
children.translated_text: Having abandoned the dualistic world, beginning with the great principle, expanded in name only,

children.text: vihāya śuddhabodhasya kiṃ kṛtyam avaśiṣyate ||
children.translated_text: what duty remains for pure consciousness?

children.text: bhramabhūtam idaṃ sarvaṃ kiṃcin nāstīti niścayī
children.translated_text: The one certain that all this is made of illusion and that nothing at all exists

children.text: alakṣyasphuraṇaḥ śuddhaḥ svabhāvenaiva śāmyati ||
children.translated_text: is pure, with an imperceptible radiance, and becomes peaceful by his very nature.

children.text: śuddhasphuraṇarūpasya dṛśyabhāvam apaśyataḥ
children.translated_text: For one whose form is pure radiance and who does not see the state of visible objects,

children.text: kva vidhiḥ kva ca vairāgyaṃ kva tyāgaḥ kva śamo 'pi vā ||
children.translated_text: where is injunction, where dispassion, where renunciation, or where even tranquility?

children.text: sphurato 'nantarūpeṇa prakṛtiṃ ca na paśyataḥ
children.translated_text: For one shining as the infinite form and not seeing <s>prakṛti</s> (primordial nature),

children.text: kva bandhaḥ kva ca vā mokṣaḥ kva harṣaḥ kva viṣāditā ||
children.translated_text: where is bondage, where liberation, where joy, and where dejection?

children.text: buddhiparyantasaṃsāre māyāmātraṃ vivartate
children.translated_text: In <s>saṃsāra</s>, extending as far as the intellect, only <s>māyā</s> (illusion) appears as transformation;

children.text: nirmamo nirahaṅkāro niṣkāmaḥ śobhate budhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the wise one, without possessiveness, without ego, and desireless, shines.

children.text: akṣayaṃ gatasantāpam ātmānaṃ paśyato muneḥ
children.translated_text: For the sage who sees the self as imperishable and free from distress,

children.text: kva vidyā ca kva vā viśvaṃ kva deho 'haṃ mameti vā ||
children.translated_text: where is knowledge, where the world, where the body, or where 'I' and 'mine'?

children.text: nirodhādīni karmāṇi jahāti jaḍadhīr yadi
children.translated_text: If the dull-minded man abandons practices such as restraint,

children.text: manorathān pralāpāṃś ca kartum āpnoty atatkṣaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: he immediately comes to make fantasies and idle talk.

children.text: mandaḥ śrutvāpi tadvastu na jahāti vimūḍhatām
children.translated_text: Even after hearing that reality, the dull man does not abandon delusion;

children.text: nirvikalpo bahiryatnād antarviṣayalālasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: outwardly he is without conceptualization through effort, but inwardly he longs for sense-objects.

children.text: jñānād galitakarmā yo lokadṛṣṭyāpi karmakṛt
children.translated_text: He whose actions have fallen away through knowledge, though in the view of the world he still performs actions,

children.text: nāpnoty avasaraṃ kartuṃ vaktum eva na kiṃcana ||
children.translated_text: does not find an occasion to do anything, or even to say anything.

children.text: kva tamaḥ kva prakāśo vā hānaṃ kva ca na kiṃcana
children.translated_text: Where is darkness, where light, where abandonment, and where anything at all

children.text: nirvikārasya dhīrasya nirātaṅkasya sarvadā ||
children.translated_text: for the steadfast one who is always changeless and free from fear?

children.text: kva dhairyaṃ kva vivekitvaṃ kva nirātaṅkatāpi vā
children.translated_text: Where is courage, where discriminating wisdom, or where even freedom from fear

children.text: anirvācyasvabhāvasya niḥsvabhāvasya yoginaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for the yogin whose nature is indescribable and who is without fixed nature?

children.text: na svargo naiva narako jīvanmuktir na caiva hi
children.translated_text: There is no heaven, no hell, and indeed no liberation while living;

children.text: bahunātra kim uktena yogadṛṣṭyā na kiṃcana ||
children.translated_text: what more need be said here? From the yogic point of view, there is nothing at all.

children.text: naiva prārthayate lābhaṃ nālābhenānuśocati
children.translated_text: He does not pray for gain, nor does he grieve over non-gain;

children.text: dhīrasya śītalaṃ cittam amṛtenaiva pūritam ||
children.translated_text: the mind of the steadfast one is cool, as if filled with nectar.

children.text: na śāntaṃ stauti niṣkāmo na duṣṭam api nindati
children.translated_text: The desireless one does not praise the peaceful, nor does he blame even the wicked.

children.text: samaduḥkhasukhas tṛptaḥ kiṃcit kṛtyaṃ na paśyati ||
children.translated_text: Satisfied, equal in pain and pleasure, he sees no task at all.

children.text: dhīro na dveṣṭi saṃsāram ātmānaṃ na didṛkṣati
children.translated_text: The steadfast one does not hate <s>saṃsāra</s>, nor does he wish to see the self.

children.text: harṣāmarṣavinirmukto na mṛto na ca jīvati ||
children.translated_text: Freed from joy and resentment, he is not dead and does not live.

children.text: niḥsnehaḥ putradārādau niṣkāmo viṣayeṣu ca
children.translated_text: Without affection for sons, wives, and the like, and desireless toward sense-objects,

children.text: niścintaḥ svaśarīre 'pi nirāśaḥ śobhate budhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: free from anxiety even about his own body, without expectation, the wise one shines.

children.text: tuṣṭiḥ sarvatra dhīrasya yathāpatitavartinaḥ
children.translated_text: Contentment is everywhere for the steadfast one, who lives with whatever happens to fall to him,

children.text: svacchandaṃ carato deśān yatrāstamitaśāyinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: wandering through regions as he pleases and lying down wherever the sun has set.

children.text: patatūdetu vā deho nāsya cintā mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Whether the body falls or rises, this great-souled one has no concern for it.

children.text: svabhāvabhūmiviśrāntivismṛtāśeṣasaṃsṛteḥ ||
children.translated_text: For him who rests on the ground of his own nature, all saṃsāra has been forgotten.

children.text: akiṃcanaḥ kāmacāro nirdvandvaś chinnasaṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: Owning nothing, moving according to his desire, free from pairs of opposites and with doubt cut off,

children.text: asaktaḥ sarvabhāveṣu kevalo ramate budhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: unattached to all states of being, alone, the awakened one delights.

children.text: nirmamaḥ śobhate dhīraḥ samaloṣṭāśmakāñcanaḥ
children.translated_text: The steadfast one, without possessiveness and regarding clod, stone, and gold alike, shines.

children.text: subhinnahṛdayagranthir vinirdhūtarajastamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The knot of his heart is thoroughly split, and rajas and tamas have been completely shaken off.

children.text: sarvatrānavadhānasya na kiṃcid vāsanā hṛdi
children.translated_text: For one who is inattentive everywhere, there is no trace of latent desire in the heart.

children.text: muktātmano vitṛptasya tulanā kena jāyate ||
children.translated_text: With what can the liberated self, fully satisfied, be compared?

children.text: jānann api na jānāti paśyann api na paśyati
children.translated_text: Though knowing, he does not know; though seeing, he does not see.

children.text: bruvann api na ca brūte ko 'nyo nirvāsanād ṛte ||
children.translated_text: Though speaking, he does not speak. Who else is like this, apart from one without latent desire?

children.text: bhikṣur vā bhūpatir vāpi yo niṣkāmaḥ sa śobhate
children.translated_text: Whether a mendicant or even a king, one who is desireless shines.

children.text: bhāveṣu galitā yasya śobhanāśobhanā matiḥ ||
children.translated_text: His judgment about good and bad has melted away among all states of being.

children.text: kva svācchandyaṃ kva saṅkocaḥ kva vā tattvaviniścayaḥ
children.translated_text: Where is self-will, where restraint, and where indeed any ascertainment of reality

children.text: nirvyājārjavabhūtasya caritārthasya yoginaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for the yogin who has become guileless straightforwardness and whose purpose is fulfilled?

children.text: ātmaviśrāntitṛptena nirāśena gatārtinā
children.translated_text: For one satisfied by resting in the self, without expectation and rid of distress,

children.text: antar yad anubhūyeta tat kathaṃ kasya kathyate ||
children.translated_text: how, and to whom, can what is experienced within be told?

children.text: supto 'pi na suṣuptau ca svapne 'pi śayito na ca
children.translated_text: Even asleep he is not in deep sleep, and even in a dream he is not lying down.

children.text: jāgare 'pi na jāgarti dhīras tṛptaḥ pade pade ||
children.translated_text: Even in waking he does not wake; the steadfast one is satisfied at every step.

children.text: jñaḥ sacinto 'pi niścintaḥ sendriyo 'pi nirindriyaḥ
children.translated_text: The knower, though with thought, is without thought; though with senses, he is without senses.

children.text: sabuddhir api nirbuddhiḥ sāhaṅkāro 'nahaṃkṛtiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Though with intellect, he is without intellect; though with ego, he has no ego-making.

children.text: na sukhī na ca vā duḥkhī na virakto na saṅgavān
children.translated_text: He is not happy and not unhappy, not detached and not attached.

children.text: na mumukṣur na vā mukto na kiṃcin na ca kiṃcana ||
children.translated_text: He is not a seeker of liberation, nor liberated; not anything, and not nothing.

children.text: vikṣepe 'pi na vikṣiptaḥ samādhau na samādhimān
children.translated_text: Even amid distraction he is not distracted; in <s>samādhi</s> he is not one possessing <s>samādhi</s>.

children.text: jāḍye 'pi na jaḍo dhanyaḥ pāṇḍitye 'pi na paṇḍitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even in dullness the blessed one is not dull; even in learning he is not learned.

children.text: mukto yathāsthitisvasthaḥ kṛtakartavyanirvṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: The liberated one, healthy in himself just as things stand, is at peace because what had to be done has been done.

children.text: samaḥ sarvatra vaitṛṣṇyān na smaraty akṛtaṃ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Equal everywhere because of freedom from thirst, he does not remember what has not been done or what has been done.

children.text: na prīyate vandyamāno nindyamāno na kupyati
children.translated_text: He is not pleased when honored, and when blamed he is not angry.

children.text: naivodvijati maraṇe jīvane nābhinandati ||
children.translated_text: He is not disturbed at death, nor does he rejoice in life.

children.text: na dhāvati janākīrṇaṃ nāraṇyam upaśāntadhīḥ
children.translated_text: His understanding pacified, he does not run toward a crowded place or toward the forest.

children.text: yathātathā yatratatra sama evāvatiṣṭhate ||
children.translated_text: In whatever way, wherever he is, he remains exactly the same.

children.text: Chapter 19
janaka uvāca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Janaka</s> said:

children.text: tattvavijñānasandaṃśam ādāya hṛdayodarāt
children.translated_text: Taking up the pincers of knowledge of reality from the cavity of the heart,

children.text: nānāvidhaparāmarśaśalyoddhāraḥ kṛto mayā ||
children.translated_text: I have extracted the thorns of many kinds of deliberation.

children.text: kva dharmaḥ kva ca vā kāmaḥ kva cārthaḥ kva vivekitā
children.translated_text: Where is <s>dharma</s> (normative duty), where is desire, where is wealth, and where is discrimination?

children.text: kva dvaitaṃ kva ca vādvaitaṃ svamahimni sthitasya me ||
children.translated_text: Where is duality, and where indeed is nonduality, for me who am established in my own greatness?

children.text: kva bhūtaṃ kva bhaviṣyad vā vartamānam api kva vā
children.translated_text: Where is the past, or where the future, and where even the present?

children.text: kva deśaḥ kva ca vā nityaṃ svamahimni sthitasya me ||
children.translated_text: Where is place, and where indeed is the eternal, for me who am established in my own greatness?

children.text: kva cātmā kva ca vānātmā kva śubhaṃ kvāśubhaṃ yathā
children.translated_text: Where is the self, and where is the non-self? Where is good, where is bad, and in what manner?

children.text: kva cintā kva ca vācintā svamahimni sthitasya me ||
children.translated_text: Where is thought, and where indeed is absence of thought, for me who am established in my own greatness?

children.text: kva svapnaḥ kva suṣuptir vā kva ca jāgaraṇaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Where is dream, where is deep sleep, and likewise where is waking?

children.text: kva turiyaṃ bhayaṃ vāpi svamahimni sthitasya me ||
children.translated_text: Where is the fourth state, or even fear, for me who am established in my own greatness?

children.text: kva dūraṃ kva samīpaṃ vā bāhyaṃ kvābhyantaraṃ kva vā
children.translated_text: Where is far, where is near, where is external, and where internal?

children.text: kva sthūlaṃ kva ca vā sūkṣmaṃ svamahimni sthitasya me ||
children.translated_text: Where is gross, and where indeed is subtle, for me who am established in my own greatness?

children.text: kva mṛtyurjīvitaṃ vā kva lokāḥ kvāsya kva laukikam
children.translated_text: Where is death, where life, where are the worlds, and where is this worldly realm?

children.text: kva layaḥ kva samādhir vā svamahimni sthitasya me ||
children.translated_text: Where is dissolution, or where is <s>samādhi</s>, for me who am established in my own greatness?

children.text: alaṃ trivargakathayā yogasya kathayāpy alam
children.translated_text: Enough of talk about the three aims of life; enough even of talk about yoga.

children.text: alaṃ vijñānakathayā viśrāntasya mamātmani ||
children.translated_text: Enough of talk about knowledge, for me who rest in the self.

children.text: Chapter 20
janaka uvāca
children.translated_text: <s>Janaka</s> said:

children.text: kva bhūtāni kva deho vā kvendriyāṇi kva vā manaḥ
children.translated_text: Where are the elements, or where is the body? Where are the senses, and where is the mind?

children.text: kva śūnyaṃ kva ca nairāśyaṃ matsvarūpe nirañjane ||
children.translated_text: Where is emptiness, and where is despair, in my stainless own form?

children.text: kva śāstraṃ kvātmavijñānaṃ kva vā nirviṣayaṃ manaḥ
children.translated_text: Where is scripture, where is knowledge of the self, and where is the mind free from objects?

children.text: kva tṛptiḥ kva vitṛṣṇatvaṃ gatadvandvasya me sadā ||
children.translated_text: Where is satisfaction, where is freedom from thirst, for me who am always beyond dualities?

children.text: kva vidyā kva ca vāvidyā kvāhaṃ kvedaṃ mama kva vā
children.translated_text: Where is knowledge, and where ignorance? Where am I, where is this, and where is mine?

children.text: kva bandhaḥ kva ca vā mokṣaḥ svarūpasya kva rūpitā ||
children.translated_text: Where is bondage, and where liberation? What form can there be for one's own true nature?

children.text: kva prārabdhāni karmāṇi jīvanmuktir api kva vā
children.translated_text: Where are the actions that have begun to bear fruit, and where even liberation while living?

children.text: kva tad videhakaivalyaṃ nirviśeṣasya sarvadā ||
children.translated_text: Where is that bodiless isolation, for one who is always without distinctions?

children.text: kva kartā kva ca vā bhoktā niṣkriyaṃ sphuraṇaṃ kva vā
children.translated_text: Where is the agent, and where the experiencer? Where is inactive radiance?

children.text: kvāparokṣaṃ phalaṃ vā kva niḥsvabhāvasya me sadā ||
children.translated_text: Where is direct perception, and where is its fruit, for me who am always without intrinsic nature?

children.text: kva lokaḥ kva mumukṣur vā kva yogī jñānavān kva vā
children.translated_text: Where is the world, and where a seeker of liberation? Where is a yogin, and where one possessing knowledge?

children.text: kva baddhaḥ kva ca vā muktaḥ svasvarūpe 'ham advaye ||
children.translated_text: Where is one bound, and where indeed one liberated, when I am in my own nondual form?

children.text: kva sṛṣṭiḥ kva ca saṃhāraḥ kva sādhyaṃ kva ca sādhanam
children.translated_text: Where is creation, and where dissolution? Where is what is to be accomplished, and where the means?

children.text: kva sādhakaḥ kva siddhir vā svasvarūpe 'ham advaye ||
children.translated_text: Where is the practitioner, and where attainment, when I am in my own nondual form?

children.text: kva pramātā pramāṇaṃ vā kva prameyaṃ kva ca pramā
children.translated_text: Where is the knower, or the means of knowledge? Where is the object known, and where is knowledge?

children.text: kva kiṃcit kva na kiṃcid vā sarvadā vimalasya me ||
children.translated_text: Where is anything, or where is nothing, for me who am always stainless?

children.text: kva vikṣepaḥ kva caikāgryaṃ kva nirbodhaḥ kva mūḍhatā
children.translated_text: Where is distraction, and where one-pointedness? Where is lack of understanding, and where delusion?

children.text: kva harṣaḥ kva viṣādo vā sarvadā niṣkriyasya me ||
children.translated_text: Where is joy, and where sorrow, for me who am always actionless?

children.text: kva caiṣa vyavahāro vā kva ca sā paramārthatā
children.translated_text: Where is this practical dealing, and where that ultimate reality?

children.text: kva sukhaṃ kva ca vā duḥkhaṃ nirvimarśasya me sadā ||
children.translated_text: Where is happiness, and where indeed suffering, for me who am always without reflective discrimination?

children.text: kva māyā kva ca saṃsāraḥ kva prītir viratiḥ kva vā
children.translated_text: Where is illusion, and where saṃsāra? Where is affection, and where dispassion?

children.text: kva jīvaḥ kva ca tadbrahma sarvadā vimalasya me ||
children.translated_text: Where is the individual soul, and where that <s>brahman</s>, for me who am always stainless?

children.text: kva pravṛttir nirvṛttir vā kva muktiḥ kva ca bandhanam
children.translated_text: Where is activity, or cessation? Where is liberation, and where bondage

children.text: kūṭasthanirvibhāgasya svasthasya mama sarvadā ||
children.translated_text: for me who am immutable, without division, self-abiding always?

children.text: kvopadeśaḥ kva vā śāstraṃ kva śiṣyaḥ kva ca vā guruḥ
children.translated_text: Where is instruction, and where scripture? Where is the disciple, and where the teacher?

children.text: kva cāsti puruṣārtho vā nirupādheḥ śivasya me ||
children.translated_text: And where is there any human goal, for me who am without limiting adjuncts and auspicious?

children.text: kva cāsti kva ca vā nāsti kvāsti caikaṃ kva ca dvayam
children.translated_text: Where is there anything, and where indeed is there nothing? Where is there one, and where is there two?

children.text: bahunātra kim uktena kiṃcin nottiṣṭhate mama ||
children.translated_text: What is the use of saying much here? Nothing at all arises for me.
